# RDKit InChI Full Source Port Plan

## Execution Contract

- This plan is for sequential continuous execution.
- "Sequential continuous execution" means execute one step at a time in order and continue to the next unchecked step until all steps are completed, blocked, or the user interrupts.
- It does not mean executing steps in unordered batches or postponing validation for a batch of changes.
- Execute unchecked steps in order.
- Continue executing the plan until all steps are completed, blocked, or the user interrupts.
- Do not stop after every step unless the plan explicitly says to stop.
- Mark each completed step by changing only its `[ ]` to `[x]`.
- Never execute unchecked steps out of order.
- Never summarize, skip, or reinterpret later unchecked steps.
- Never treat a required reading step as “already read”.
- Do not assume the agent is diligent.
- Do not assume the model context is long enough.
- Do not rely on memory from previous turns when a required reading step is present.
- Every real task step must be immediately preceded by reading `dev/policy_invariants.md` and `dev/source_reproduction_protocol.md`.
- The reading step must explicitly reload and follow the required execution standard, source reproduction rules, artifact requirements, no-git rule, and completion criteria for the next task.
- `Implement`, `Port`, `Modify`, `Update`, and `Fix` steps must produce a concrete artifact.
- `Audit` steps must produce a written gap report and must not replace later implementation steps.
- If a step adds or updates tests, the next real task after the required reading step must run the most specific relevant test command for those tests.
- Final whole-plan validation is required after all source-backed implementation steps.
- Copying comments, adding a dispatch stub, adding an FFI declaration, or adding a placeholder return is not a completed port step.
- No production InChI API may be exposed until its selected source call graph is fully implemented and tested.
- No SMILES, formula, MolBlock regeneration, external command, Open Babel call, or similarity-based fallback may stand in for InChI behavior.
- During porting, do not execute any git operation unless the human author explicitly requests it.

## Scope Decision

This is a full source port, not an adapter-only integration. The reusable
`cosmolkit-inchi` crate must not depend on `cosmolkit-core`, RDKit, Python,
Open Babel, a system InChI library, or an external executable.

The pinned RDKit adapter and the official InChI C implementation may be used
as source references and independent golden oracles. A native C FFI may be
used only in a non-production oracle tool if it is required to generate
goldens; that tool must not be the implementation under test.

The RDKit submodule contains `External/INCHI-API/inchi.cpp` and headers, but
not the official InChI engine under `External/INCHI-API/src`. Acquiring and
legally pinning that engine as its own submodule is therefore a hard
prerequisite. If the exact source cannot be pinned and redistributed under an
approved license, the plan stops with the feature explicitly unsupported.

The submodule and crate boundary must follow the existing
`third_party/RingDecomposerLib` plus `cosmolkit-ringdecomposer` model:

- add the complete upstream source tree as a pinned Git submodule at
  `third_party/InChI`;
- record the upstream repository, release or tag, commit, checksum, and local
  source path in `crates/cosmolkit-inchi/README.md`;
- keep the upstream license beside the upstream source;
- copy each corresponding C function body into its Rust function using
  `BEGIN INCHI C FUNCTION` and `END INCHI C FUNCTION` frames;
- use `INCHI` as the two-axis source-marker prefix;
- expose only toolkit-neutral graph and InChI data types from the reusable
  crate;
- keep the COSMolKit `Molecule` conversion in `cosmolkit-core`.

`third_party/rdkit/External/INCHI-API/inchi.cpp` remains a separate RDKit
adapter source. Its copied blocks use `RDKit` markers, not `INCHI` markers.
The official engine and the RDKit adapter must never be collapsed into one
untraceable implementation.

## Function-Inventory Regeneration Gate

This revision is a pre-inventory bootstrap plan. Step 11 is a hard plan
replacement gate: it must replace every Step 12 and later with a newly
numbered, function-level execution plan derived from the pinned submodule
inventory. No Step 12 or later in this revision may be executed or checked.
The downstream steps currently present only record required integration and
validation coverage; they are not permission to port a source-file group in a
single step.

The regenerated plan must give each official InChI C function its own `Port`
step. Each allocation/free function, normalization helper, canonicalization
helper, stereo helper, ring helper, parser, printer, option helper, key helper,
and public engine entry point must be named exactly as it appears in the pinned
source inventory. Wildcards such as `*`, phrases such as "all functions", and
source-file or subsystem-wide `Port` steps are invalid.

The regenerated plan must also give each RDKit adapter function its own `Port`
step, including at least:

- `assignBondDirs`;
- `findAlternatingBonds`;
- `_Valence4NCleanUp1` and `_Valence4NCleanUp2`;
- `_Valence5NCleanUp1` through `_Valence5NCleanUp9`;
- `_Valence5NCleanUpA` and `_Valence5NCleanUpB`;
- `_Valence7SCleanUp1`, `_Valence7SCleanUp2`, and `_Valence7SCleanUp3`;
- `_Valence8SCleanUp1`;
- `_Valence8ClCleanUp1`, `_Valence5ClCleanUp1`, and
  `_Valence3ClCleanUp1`;
- `cleanUp`;
- `fixOptionSymbol`;
- `rCleanUp`;
- `InchiToMol`;
- `MolToInchi`;
- `MolBlockToInchi`;
- `InchiToInchiKey`;
- the inline `MolToInchiKey` adapter from `inchi.h`;
- `getInchiVersion`.

For every function-level test-writing step, the regenerated plan must place
the corresponding focused test command after the mandatory protocol-reading
step. Aggregated parity suites remain final validation and cannot replace
those focused commands.

## Reusable Crate Boundary

The reusable crate owns toolkit-neutral atom, bond, coordinate, isotope,
radical, hydrogen, stereo, status, diagnostics, option, AuxInfo, InChIKey,
engine, and adapter behavior. It does not own COSMolKit `Molecule`, operation
registry, cache, Python, or PyO3 types. It has no native-library, subprocess,
network, SMILES, or MolBlock regeneration dependency.

## Regenerated Function-Level Execution Contract

- Official production functions are ordered callee-first from the audited source call graph.
- Every function port includes its copied source frame and a uniquely named focused test.
- Every test-writing port step is immediately followed, after the mandatory reading step, by its exact focused test command.
- For each audited mutual-recursion component, the first formal function port uses complete source-framed operation-local implementations of its unported companions; later companion steps promote those implementations and replace the local copies.
- CLI and demo functions remain inventory-only and are not production port steps.
- No production API is exposed until all official and RDKit adapter function steps pass.
